chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

This matter (the rule will not be established until no class of people remains but that they have ruled over people, so that no one may say: 'If we had ruled, we would have established justice,' then the Qa'im will rise with the truth and justice.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser (al-Qa'im), referring to the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the signs preceding the appearance of al-Qa'im regarding the rule of different classes of people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines a critical eschatological precondition: the universal failure of all social strata to establish justice, thereby nullifying the claim of any specific group to exclusive legitimacy. This 'exhaustion of justice' creates the vacuum that necessitates the rise of al-Qa'im, whose appearance is not merely a political shift but the restoration of divine equity after humanity has tested every alternative. The narration emphasizes that the Mahdi’s authority is validated by the prior failure of all other claimants to rule justly.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (53) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan from Muhammad bin Abdullah from Muhammad bin Abu Omayr from Hisham bin Salim that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“Al-Qa’im will not appear except after that every class of people will have ruled over people so that no one may say: “If we have ruled, we will have spread justice” then al-Qa’im will rise to rule with truth and justice.”
